du.name: du (system)
du.notes: GNU coreutils on Linux, BSD du on macOS (version = OS build).

ncdu.name: ncdu (JSON export)
ncdu.notes: Non-interactive export mode (-o); includes writing the JSON export.

erdtree.name: erdtree (erd)
erdtree.notes: -i/--hidden so .gitignore'd and hidden files are counted like every other tool.

nulldisk.name: NullDisk CLI
nulldisk.notes: Maintainer's own tool (see disclosure). Installed from the public manifest https://assets.nulldisk.app/releases/cli/latest.json (override with NULLDISK_CLI_MANIFEST); listed as pending while the download is not published. '--depth 0' prints only the root total (like du -s); 'size' is allocated bytes with hard links counted once (per `nulldisk scan --help`). Not available for Windows.

qdirstat.name: QDirStat
qdirstat.method: `qdirstat <dir>` under Xvfb. Completion: the app's own log (/tmp/qdirstat-$USER/qdirstat.log) gets 'Reading finished' for this process. Total: the root row's Size column, read via AT-SPI (human-readable).

k4dirstat.name: K4DirStat
k4dirstat.method: `k4dirstat <dir>` under Xvfb. Completion: status bar text becomes 'Finished. Elapsed time: …' (AT-SPI). Total: the root row's Subtree Total column, read via AT-SPI (human-readable).

planned_gui.name: OmniDiskSweeper
planned_gui.reason: Runs on macos-14, but scans of the benchmark's disk-image dataset volume are 50-75x slower than the same tree on the runner's boot disk (~115 s for the 150k-file tree vs a few seconds on the boot disk). Not caused by mount options (-nobrowse and case-sensitivity tested) or by TCC (Full Disk Access / removable-volume grants tested). Timing would measure the runner's disk-image layer rather than the app, and doesn't fit the 300-minute job budget. The harness (bench/gui/macos_app.py) and pinned install are kept for dedicated machines.

planned_gui.name: DaisyDisk
planned_gui.reason: Commercial (trial). No CLI/AppleScript scan dictionary; would need UI automation + a licence for CI. Planned for dedicated machines with the vendor's OK.

planned_gui.name: SquirrelDisk
planned_gui.reason: Open source (Tauri) and scans by spawning pdu internally, so its engine time is approximately pdu's; GUI has no completion signal. Planned.

planned_gui.name: WizTree
planned_gui.reason: Has a proper CLI export (/export=... /admin=1, MFT scan) and would be easy to automate, but the EULA allows free use for personal use only; running it on CI for a public benchmark needs a supporter licence or the vendor's permission. Planned pending permission.

planned_gui.name: TreeSize Free
planned_gui.reason: Blocked on hosted runners by its licence: TreeSize Free 4.8.1 (current download) opens a modal 'Windows Server is not supported' dialog at launch ("TreeSize Free is no longer supported on a Windows Server as of version 4.7.3") and never scans; windows-latest is Windows Server 2025. Running an older build would sidestep the vendor's terms. Planned for a Windows 10/11 (desktop) runner.

planned_gui.name: Baobab (GNOME Disk Usage Analyzer)
planned_gui.reason: Ubuntu 24.04 ships Baobab 46.0 on GTK 4.14: under Xvfb + AT-SPI the end of the scan is visible (the charts appear) but the folder list exposes no rows to AT-SPI (only its column headers) and the total is only painted in the ring chart, so the total can't be read from the app. Baobab 48 / GTK 4.18 exposes the rows and works with bench/gui/linux_atspi.py; enable when ubuntu-latest ships it.

planned_gui.name: Filelight
planned_gui.reason: Ubuntu 24.04 ships Filelight 23.08 (KF5): the status bar shows 'N files' when the scan ends, but the total size is only painted in the radial map (no accessible text, no export or CLI); under Xvfb the window even stayed on its Overview page. Planned.

planned_gui.name: dua / gdu / ncdu interactive TUIs
planned_gui.reason: Excluded: interactive mode renders to a terminal; their non-interactive modes are measured in the CLI track instead.
